complex_data_science_result: Churn model AUC=0.87; precision@10%=0.62; top drivers: tenure↓, support tickets↑, plan=Basic; lift vs baseline +31%.
human_storytelling_narrative: Our churn model now separates likely leavers from stayers with strong discrimination (AUC 0.87) and a 31% lift over the previous rule-based baseline. Focusing outreach on the top 10% risk band yields 62% precision. The main risk signals are short tenure, rising support tickets, and Basic-plan customers—so retention should prioritize early-lifecycle support and upgrade offers for Basic users.

complex_data_science_result: Revenue anomaly week 42: −18% vs 8-week MA; category Electronics −27%; region West −22%; no holiday shift; payment failures +9pp.
human_storytelling_narrative: Week 42 revenue fell 18% below the eight-week moving average, concentrated in Electronics (−27%) and the West region (−22%). The drop is not explained by holiday calendar shifts. Payment failures rose nine percentage points in the same week, pointing to a checkout or processor issue rather than demand alone. Immediate actions: audit West Electronics payment paths and restore conversion before the next campaign.

complex_data_science_result: A/B checkout test: variant B vs A; n=42k; conversion 3.4%→3.9%; relative lift +14.7%; p=0.008; no significant AOV change.
human_storytelling_narrative: Checkout variant B lifted conversion from 3.4% to 3.9% (+14.7% relative) across 42,000 sessions with a statistically significant result (p=0.008). Average order value was unchanged, so the gain is pure conversion, not basket-size inflation. Recommend shipping B to 100% traffic and monitoring payment-failure and return rates for two weeks.

complex_data_science_result: Q3 forecast: revenue $12.4M (80% PI $11.1–$13.6M); MAPE 6.2%; driver: new logo ARR +$1.1M; churn drag −$0.4M.
human_storytelling_narrative: The Q3 revenue forecast centers at $12.4M with an 80% prediction interval of $11.1–$13.6M and a recent MAPE of 6.2%. Growth is driven by roughly $1.1M in new-logo ARR, partially offset by $0.4M of churn drag. Leadership can plan near the midpoint while holding contingency for the lower bound if new-logo close rates soften.

complex_data_science_result: EDA: missing income 12%; outliers in spend >p99; correlation income↔spend r=0.61; segment High-Value = 18% of users, 54% of revenue.
human_storytelling_narrative: Exploratory analysis shows 12% missing income values and extreme spend outliers above the 99th percentile that need capping or winsorizing before modeling. Income and spend are moderately correlated (r=0.61). A High-Value segment that is only 18% of users drives 54% of revenue—retention and personalization should concentrate there first.

complex_data_science_result: Fraud model: recall@1% FPR=0.71; precision=0.44; SHAP top: device_change, geo_velocity, amount_z; false positives cost ~$2.1k/day.
human_storytelling_narrative: At a 1% false-positive rate, the fraud model recovers 71% of true fraud cases with 44% precision. The strongest signals are sudden device changes, geographic velocity spikes, and unusually large transaction amounts. Current false positives still cost about $2,100 per day, so the next iteration should tighten rules for high-value returning customers without sacrificing recall.

complex_data_science_result: NPS survey n=1,840; score 32→41 QoQ; promoters +8pp; detractors −5pp; theme clusters: shipping speed (+), app crashes (−).
human_storytelling_narrative: Net Promoter Score rose from 32 to 41 quarter over quarter among 1,840 respondents. Promoters increased eight points while detractors fell five. Theme analysis credits faster shipping for the gains and flags app crashes as the remaining pain point. Fixing crash-prone flows is the clearest path to another NPS lift.

complex_data_science_result: Funnel: visit→signup 11.2%; signup→activation 48%; activation→paid 19%; largest drop: activation→paid (−81% absolute from activated base).
human_storytelling_narrative: The funnel converts 11.2% of visits to signups and 48% of signups to activated users, but only 19% of activated users become paid. The steepest loss is therefore activation-to-paid. Monetization experiments—pricing clarity, trial length, and value-moment messaging—should target activated users before further top-of-funnel spend.

complex_data_science_result: Latency SLO: p95 API 420ms→310ms after cache; error rate 0.9%→0.3%; cache hit 78%; estimated support tickets −15%.
human_storytelling_narrative: After adding the response cache, p95 API latency improved from 420ms to 310ms and the error rate fell from 0.9% to 0.3%, with a 78% cache hit rate. We estimate roughly 15% fewer latency-related support tickets. The win validates keeping the cache and expanding it to the next hottest endpoints.

complex_data_science_result: Cohort retention D30: Jan 22%, Feb 24%, Mar 29%; feature flag 'guided_onboarding' exposure 40%; uplift +4.1pp (p=0.02).
human_storytelling_narrative: Day-30 retention climbed from 22% in January to 29% in March. Users exposed to guided onboarding (40% of the cohort) retained 4.1 percentage points higher than controls (p=0.02). Roll guided onboarding out fully and measure whether the lift holds for organic versus paid acquisition.

complex_data_science_result: Pricing elasticity: −1.2; 5% price↑ → volume −6%; revenue +≈−1.2% net; premium tier inelastic (−0.4).
human_storytelling_narrative: Overall demand elasticity is about −1.2: a 5% price increase cuts volume by roughly 6% and slightly reduces total revenue. The premium tier is far less elastic (−0.4), so selective premium increases are safer than across-the-board hikes. Prefer premium list-price tests over base-plan increases.

complex_data_science_result: Inventory stockout rate 7.8%→3.1% after reorder-point model; fill rate 91%→97%; excess stock weeks +1.2 (acceptable).
human_storytelling_narrative: The new reorder-point model cut stockouts from 7.8% to 3.1% and raised fill rate from 91% to 97%. Excess inventory rose by only 1.2 weeks of cover, which operations judged acceptable. Continue the model and refine SKU-level safety stock for the top 50 movers.

complex_data_science_result: Marketing MMM: paid search ROI 3.1; social 1.4; display 0.7; diminishing returns above $80k/wk search; recommend reallocate +$20k search from display.
human_storytelling_narrative: Marketing mix modeling estimates paid-search ROI at 3.1, social at 1.4, and display at 0.7. Search starts showing diminishing returns above about $80k per week. Reallocating roughly $20k weekly from display into search should improve efficiency without saturating the search response curve.

complex_data_science_result: Credit risk scorecard: KS=0.42; Gini=0.58; approval rate 61%; expected default 2.4%; cut-score sensitivity ±0.1 → default 2.1–2.8%.
human_storytelling_narrative: The credit scorecard separates goods and bads with KS 0.42 and Gini 0.58 at a 61% approval rate and 2.4% expected default. Moving the cut-score by ±0.1 shifts expected default between 2.1% and 2.8%. Risk appetite can be tuned within that band without rebuilding the model.

complex_data_science_result: Support tickets: volume −12% MoM; CSAT 3.8→4.2; top root cause 'password reset' −35% after UX fix; median handle time −40s.
human_storytelling_narrative: Support volume dropped 12% month over month while CSAT rose from 3.8 to 4.2. Password-reset tickets fell 35% after the UX fix, and median handle time shortened by 40 seconds. The password-reset investment is paying off; next prioritize the second-largest ticket theme.

complex_data_science_result: Recommendation offline: NDCG@10 0.41→0.48; online CTR +6.5%; diversity ↓8%; guardrail: enforce category diversity quota.
human_storytelling_narrative: The new recommender lifted offline NDCG@10 from 0.41 to 0.48 and online CTR by 6.5%, but catalog diversity fell 8%. To keep engagement gains without narrowing discovery, enforce a category diversity quota before full rollout.

complex_data_science_result: Energy usage model R²=0.81; MAPE=9.4%; peak hour error +18%; feature importance: outdoor temp, occupancy, HVAC mode.
human_storytelling_narrative: The energy usage model explains 81% of variance with a 9.4% MAPE, but peak-hour error remains about 18% high. Outdoor temperature, occupancy, and HVAC mode dominate feature importance. Improving peak forecasts should focus on better occupancy signals during business hours.

complex_data_science_result: Website SEO: organic sessions +22% YoY; ranking keywords in top-10: 180→245; bounce −3pp; content cluster 'guides' drives 38% of lift.
human_storytelling_narrative: Organic sessions grew 22% year over year as keywords in the top 10 rose from 180 to 245 and bounce rate fell three points. The guides content cluster accounts for 38% of the lift. Double down on guide refreshes and internal links from product pages into that cluster.

complex_data_science_result: Hospital readmission model AUC=0.79; calibration slope=0.94; top risk: prior admissions, polypharmacy, low follow-up adherence.
human_storytelling_narrative: The readmission model achieves AUC 0.79 with near-ideal calibration (slope 0.94). Highest risk comes from prior admissions, polypharmacy, and poor follow-up adherence. Care teams should prioritize post-discharge outreach for patients flagged on those three factors.

complex_data_science_result: Ad fraud filter: blocked 4.2% of impressions; CPA −11%; verified viewability +6pp; brand-safe inventory share 88%→93%.
human_storytelling_narrative: The ad-fraud filter blocked 4.2% of impressions and reduced cost per acquisition by 11%. Verified viewability improved six points and brand-safe inventory share rose from 88% to 93%. Keep the filter on and expand blocklists for the residual low-viewability placements.

complex_data_science_result: Supply chain ETA MAE 1.8→1.1 days; on-time delivery 82%→91%; late-penalty cost −$48k/quarter; weather feature adds +0.2 day MAE cut.
human_storytelling_narrative: ETA prediction MAE improved from 1.8 to 1.1 days and on-time delivery rose from 82% to 91%, cutting late-penalty costs by about $48k per quarter. Adding weather features contributed roughly 0.2 days of the MAE reduction. Continue weather-aware routing for lanes with high storm variance.

complex_data_science_result: Employee attrition: monthly rate 2.1%; model F1=0.69; drivers: commute>45min, low promo velocity, manager span>12; pilot retention bonus ROI 2.4x.
human_storytelling_narrative: Monthly attrition sits at 2.1%, and the attrition model reaches F1 0.69. Key drivers are long commutes, slow promotion velocity, and managers with spans above 12. A pilot retention bonus for high-risk employees returned roughly 2.4× ROI and should expand to the next two high-churn departments.

complex_data_science_result: App crash-free sessions 97.1%→99.0%; ANR 0.8%→0.3%; release 2.14; crash cluster: null deep-link params (−70% after fix).
human_storytelling_narrative: Release 2.14 raised crash-free sessions from 97.1% to 99.0% and cut ANRs from 0.8% to 0.3%. The dominant crash cluster—null deep-link parameters—dropped 70% after the fix. Stability is now within target; shift focus to performance on mid-tier Android devices.

complex_data_science_result: Customer LTV model MAPE=14%; top decile LTV 6.2× bottom; CAC payback 7→5 months after channel mix change; paid social CAC −18%.
human_storytelling_narrative: The LTV model predicts with 14% MAPE, and the top LTV decile is worth 6.2× the bottom decile. After shifting channel mix, CAC payback shortened from seven to five months and paid-social CAC fell 18%. Acquire more aggressively in channels that feed the top two LTV deciles.

complex_data_science_result: AB test email subject: open rate 18%→24%; CTR 2.1%→2.6%; revenue/email +19%; holdout confirms lift; spam complaints unchanged at 0.02%.
human_storytelling_narrative: The new subject-line variant lifted open rate from 18% to 24% and CTR from 2.1% to 2.6%, raising revenue per email by 19%. A holdout confirmed the lift, and spam complaints stayed flat at 0.02%. Adopt the winning subject pattern for lifecycle campaigns and keep monitoring complaint rates.
